hints: Notice the fuel use is $1.5 \times 10^4 \text{ cm}^3$ per hour and each $1.0 \text{ cm}^3$ supplies $34 \text{ kJ}$ - first find total energy supplied in one hour.
Remember power is energy per time in $\text{W}$ or $\text{kW}$, so the hourly energy must be divided by $3600 \text{ s}$ to get input power.
Use conservation of energy for the engine: input power equals useful power plus wasted power, with useful power given as $40 \text{ kW}$.
walkthrough: Find total chemical energy supplied per hour: $E = 1.5 \times 10^4 \times 34 \text{ kJ} = 5.1 \times 10^5 \text{ kJ}$.
Convert to joules: $5.1 \times 10^5 \text{ kJ} = 5.1 \times 10^8 \text{ J}$ supplied in $3600 \text{ s}$.
Find input power with $P = E/t$: $P_{in} = 5.1 \times 10^8 / 3600 \approx 1.42 \times 10^5 \text{ W} \approx 142 \text{ kW}$.
Apply energy conservation: $P_{in} = P_{useful} + P_{wasted}$, so $P_{wasted} = P_{in} - P_{useful}$.
Substitute values: $P_{wasted} \approx 142 \text{ kW} - 40 \text{ kW} \approx 102 \text{ kW}$. This is option A.

options.A: Input power about $142 \text{ kW}$ minus $40 \text{ kW}$ useful leaves about $102 \text{ kW}$ wasted.
options.B: About $142 \text{ kW}$ is the total input power from the fuel, before subtracting the $40 \text{ kW}$ useful output.
options.C: About $182 \text{ kW}$ adds the input and useful powers instead of using input power minus useful power.
options.D: About $470 \text{ kW}$ comes from not converting per hour to per second when finding power in $\text{kW}$.
